title: Skej
tagline: Skej - Zk-native, privacy-first ENS Scheduling Infra for Consumers and AI Agents on Zirkuit
description:
Skej is a decentralized scheduling protocol that enables privacy-preserving meeting coordination between ENS addresses using ZK proofs on Zircuit, with token payments for premium scheduling features and AI agent services, envisioned as the Stripe API for 'time'.

Skej solves the trillion-dollar scheduling coordination problem with Web3 principles while creating the first privacy-first scheduling infrastructure specifically designed for the emerging AI agent economy - leveraging all of Zircuit's unique capabilities such as fast and cheap transactions with Ethereum security.
how_its_made:
This project is currently a concept vision on Zirkuit.

Skej is a privacy-preserving scheduling protocol on Zircuit enabling ENS addresses to coordinate meetings through zero-knowledge proofs. Users can find mutual availability without revealing full calendar data, while tokens enable premium features and AI agent payments.

Built specifically for Zircuit's capabilities: sequencer security prevents scheduling spam, account abstraction provides gasless UX, and low-cost transactions ($0.01 vs $50+ on L1) make frequent AI agent interactions viable. The protocol combines ZK availability matching, decentralized coordination via blockchain events, and IPFS storage for encrypted calendar data.

Targets the $3.5B global scheduling software market, focusing initially on 5M+ ENS domain owners and AI developers building scheduling automation. Addresses the $541B annual loss from scheduling inefficiencies while creating new economic opportunities in the emerging $50B+ AI agent economy.

Core implementation includes basic privacy-preserving meeting coordination, token integration, and foundational smart contracts - establishing the infrastructure for decentralized scheduling coordination.
